[I]Supreme Chancellor Anika Rau is losing the support of even her own party.[/i]
The leader of the Unity Front for Progress and Supreme Chancellor of Velmara, Anika Rau, faced immense pressure from Parliament to resign after she failed to pass a bill titled Criminal Punishment Resort. The bill would legalise harsher criminal punishments, to try and dissuade people from breaking the law. In 2024, the UFP won 263 out of 500 seats in the National Assembly, 3 of whom have defected to PRP and HFM respectfully, but would still expect to be able to pass legislation in Parliament. Only 83 of the 260 UFP MPs voted in favour, joined by 5 MPs from other parties, leaving the bill failed. This has led to questions over Raus leadership and a vote of no confidence could be held in the coming weeks.
